name: LFM2.5-24B-A2B
pitch: LiquidAI's fast chat model, a mixture of 64 experts with short convolutions, about 2B parameters a token.
architecture: 40 layers, 30 double-gated short convolutions and 10 grouped-query attention layers, with a mixture of 64 experts of which 4 run a token in 38 of them (two dense layers first); it always thinks before it answers and calls tools in a Pythonic list.
license: The model's license (LFM Open License v1.0) is on its Hugging Face page. TandemLLM itself is AGPL-3.0 or commercial.

measurements.method: tools/fn_lookup_ab.py through one fresh server a run on the Spark, the GPU to itself (the conversion queue paused): prompts prose / chat / code, one greedy request each, thinking off, 512 new tokens, conductor raw, one slot, max_len 32,768. 4.0 as its profile serves it: the lookup alone cut by StairCut, with the suffix store off so no earlier answer is in it, the dense splits of ops/lfm25-dense-splits.json; BF16 plain (--drafter none). One run a cell.
measurements.source: SPD-107 window runs, 2026-10-14 06:52 (4.0, default-calibration pack) and 05:10 (BF16); raw data spark ~/lfm25/runs/dbg/ab-look.json, ~/lfm25/runs/w7/ab-none-bf16.json

rows.note: Each text equal to the plain run's (143.7 / 142.3 / 143.4 tok/s plain). The same run's edit and copy asks (a file back with a name renamed, a text back unchanged) took 222.0 and 292.2 tok/s, 3.43 and 10.65 tokens a block, against 141.5 and 141.6 plain.
Plain decode (--drafter none); the BF16 projections run on the 16-row tile GEMM, the experts a pair at a time.

parts.label: Allocator reserve
parts.source: an estimate until measured on the Spark (SPD-107)

components.label: Conductor
components.what: Gives each request the right instructions and helper packages, and watches long sessions so they do not get stuck.
components.note: Off by default for this model (measured on 4.0, 2026-10-14): on four short chat asks its notes (1,241 to 2,714 hidden tokens) made the model think 856 to 1,437 tokens where it thought 99 to 902 without them, and with thinking off it reasoned in the answer instead of answering. Off, clients talk to the raw engine and the small models below have nothing to do.

components.label: Narrator
components.what: A small model that writes short status lines while the big model thinks, so you can see what it is doing.
components.note: Qwen3.5-2B, 3.60 GiB in the live memory split. When memory runs short it goes after the shadow reader and loads again later.

components.label: Laya decision models
components.what: Three tiny classifiers that answer the conductor's quick questions, like what kind of request this is, in milliseconds.
components.note: Without them the big model answers those questions itself, which costs a turn each time.

components.label: Response cache
components.what: Answers an identical greedy request again from memory, without running the model.
components.note: Off on the reference box. Useful for scripts that send the same request many times; never for a benchmark.

components.label: Other backends
components.what: Lets the dashboard send some model names to other servers or cloud APIs, beside this engine.
components.note: You add the backends later, on the Backends screen.

components.label: Conversation cache
components.what: Keeps the conversation the model is in, so the next turn starts where the last one ended instead of reading everything again.
components.note: The resident prefix with its anchors every 4,096 tokens (the prefill's chunk), the end anchor, the pin and the park; an anchor is 80.2 MiB (240 KiB of convolution inputs and 4,096 tokens of KV at 20,480 bytes).

components.label: State store
components.what: Saves the model's state after short chats, so the same start a second time costs nothing.

methods.label: Temperature
methods.what: How random the answers are when a client does not say. Liquid recommends 0.1 for this model.

methods.label: Top-k
methods.what: How many of the likeliest next tokens a sampled answer draws from, when a client does not say.

methods.label: Repetition penalty
methods.what: How much the model is kept from repeating itself, when a client does not say. 1 is off.

methods.label: Default answer length
methods.what: The longest answer, in tokens, when a client does not set max_tokens.

methods.label: Request time limit
methods.what: Seconds one request may run before the engine stops it.

methods.label: Queue length
methods.what: How many requests may wait for a free slot before new ones are turned away.

methods.label: Queue wait
methods.what: Seconds a request may wait in the queue before it gets an error.

advanced.label: Port
advanced.what: The port the API and the dashboard answer on.

advanced.label: Listen on
advanced.what: The whole network, or only this machine.

advanced.label: Raw engine name
advanced.what: The model name of the raw engine. With the conductor on, clients see TandemLLM and this name is a hidden alias.

advanced.label: Dashboard login
advanced.what: With an admin password set, on makes the dashboard ask for it too.

advanced.label: Admin password
advanced.what: Without one, anyone who reaches the port can change the setup. Generate writes a random one into secrets.env on the box; read it there with cat.
